correctness.rationale: Factoring the printed Eq. (3.1) gives the weighted-endpoint identity exactly and differentiation gives the monotonicity law. Full primary-source inspection confirms Eq. (3.1), Table 2 \(\beta_2=4.9\times10^{-7}\), and the printed \(v\approx0.023\) threshold claim. Direct high-precision substitution gives \(R_S\approx44272.53\) and \(R_V\approx2.66178>1\); therefore every convex combination is supercritical. The Figure 1 parameter statement gives \(R_0\approx3.66948\); the infected \((E,A)\) Jacobian block has negative determinant and therefore one positive eigenvalue.
residual_risks: The audit concerns the published equations and printed decimal parameters, not undocumented simulation inputs.

value.rationale: The correction invalidates a concrete policy threshold and a disease-free stability claim in a published epidemiological model. The endpoint decomposition also supplies the exact condition under which vaccination alone can ever cross threshold, so the result is substantively motivated despite elementary algebra.
residual_risks: No claim is made about global endemic dynamics for \(R_0>1\).

final_claim: For the printed Ihsanjaya--Susyanto model, \(R_0(v)=(\mu R_S+vR_V)/(\mu+v)\); hence vaccination can cross below one from \(R_S>1\) only if \(R_V<1\). The paper's Table 2 has \(R_V>1\), so no vaccination rate is subcritical, its reported \(v\approx0.023\) threshold is incompatible with Eq. (3.1), and its stated Figure 1 disease-free parameter set is linearly unstable.
scientific_limitations: Only the printed mathematical specification is audited; undocumented simulation inputs are unknown.
